_about: Pose lists for every strip in sheets/, reconstructed from the prompts that produced them (2026-11-19). Same pose text; the surrounding wording now comes from config/character.json. 'rule' is a rule that applies to every pose.

_generation.reference: None for the first strip. After that, one pinned image of the character, and the words 'use only for appearance, ignore the poses'. Prone exercises: pin a standing strip, not a lying one.
_generation.credits_each: about 1,218 without a reference, 1,827 with one (ElevenLabs, 2026-11-19)

toe-touch-c1.layout: Same scale, feet on the same invisible floor line, with wide empty gaps so the figures never touch.
poses: START: standing tall, feet about shoulder-width apart, both arms straight up overhead, upper arms beside the ears.
FOLD: deep forward bend, torso folded down toward the legs, knees only slightly bent (not forced straight, not deeply squatting), fingertips touching the floor beside the feet, head hanging relaxed.
STRETCH BACK: standing again with arms still stretched up and reaching backward, a gentle backward bend, hips pushed slightly forward, chest and face lifted toward the sky, knees straight.
learned: Take 2's backward bend swept the arms down behind him; the booklet says up and back. Take 1 kept the arms up and reaching back.
The model draws a ground shadow even when told not to; the key removes it.

partial-sit-up-c1.layout: In every pose he lies on his back with his HEAD ON THE LEFT and his FEET ON THE RIGHT, same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps so the figures never touch.
poses: START: lying flat on his back, LEGS STRAIGHT and flat on the floor with the feet a few inches apart, arms straight and resting at his sides.
LIFTING: head and shoulders lifted clear off the floor, chin slightly tucked, arms reaching forward along his sides, LEGS STILL STRAIGHT AND FLAT.

TOP: upper body raised only far enough that he can see his heels, looking down toward his feet, arms reaching forward toward the shins, LEGS STAY COMPLETELY STRAIGHT with heels on the floor (knees NOT bent, NOT sitting fully upright, hands NOT behind the head).
learned: Take 1 bent the knees at the top: the booklet says keep the legs straight. Always include 'knees NOT bent' and 'NOT sitting fully upright, hands NOT behind the head'.
Takes 2 and 3 sat almost fully upright. Take 4 lifted only the head and shoulders in the middle pose.

alternate-leg-raise-c1.kept: retry take 1 of 4 (first batch failed: push-up arms leaked in from the reference)
alternate-leg-raise-c1.layout: In every pose he lies FACE DOWN, flat on his belly, with his HEAD ON THE RIGHT looking right and his FEET ON THE LEFT. Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps between figures.
alternate-leg-raise-c1.rule: KEY BODY RULE FOR ALL THREE POSES: his arms are NOT pushing up and NOT planted in front of him. Both arms are STRAIGHT and stretched back along his sides, with the hands tucked flat, palms down, UNDER THE FRONT OF HIS THIGHS. Elbows straight. Shoulders stay low.
poses: START: lying completely flat face down, legs straight and together, chin near the floor, arms straight back with palms under the thighs.

FIRST LEG: head and chest lifted only slightly off the floor (a small lift), arms still straight back under the thighs, the leg NEAREST the viewer raised straight up behind him with the knee LOCKED STRAIGHT (a straight line from hip to heel, about 35 to 40 degrees above the floor, thigh clearly lifted off his hand), the other leg flat on the floor.
OTHER LEG: same lifted head and chest, arms still straight back under the thighs, now the leg FARTHEST from the viewer is raised with the knee LOCKED STRAIGHT, and the near leg is flat on the floor.
learned: First batch failed all four times: the push-up strip, used as the reference, leaked push-up arms and a bent kicking leg into this exercise.
Fix: use a neutral standing strip as the reference, say 'use it only for appearance, ignore its poses', and spell out the geometry (arms straight back, palms under the thighs, knee locked straight).
The darker far-side shading is what lets near leg and far leg read differently in profile.

knee-push-up-c1.kept: take 4 of 4 of the no-reference pilot (this one became the first character reference)
knee-push-up-c1.layout: Same scale, all three standing on the same invisible floor line, with generous empty space between the three figures so they do not touch or overlap.
poses: DOWN position: face-down, chest touching the floor, elbows bent and tucked close to the ribs, palms flat on the floor directly under the shoulders. The KNEES are on the floor and the lower legs are bent up behind him with the feet in the air. Body is a straight line from the knees to the head.
MIDDLE position: halfway up, elbows bent about 90 degrees, chest a hand-width above the floor, knees still on the floor, body still a straight line from knees to head.

UP position: arms fully straightened, palms flat on the floor directly under the shoulders, upper body raised, KNEES STILL ON THE FLOOR, lower legs bent up behind with feet in the air, body one straight diagonal line from the knees to the head (hips NOT piked up, back NOT sagging).
learned: This was the pilot: no reference image, the character described in words. It came out right in all four takes.
Take 4 was kept because the chest actually touches the floor at the bottom and the arms are fully straight at the top. Then it became the first character reference.

stationary-run-c1.kept: retry take 3 of 4 (first batch lifted the same leg twice)
stationary-run-c1.layout: Same scale, same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps. He does not travel forward: jogging on the spot with small quick steps, the lifted foot only a few inches off the floor, knee bent only slightly, NOT a sprint stride, NOT high knees, NOT a long stride. Arms bent about 90 degrees and pumping like a jogger.
stationary-run-c1.rule: The boy's NEAR leg and near arm are closest to the viewer, in the normal colors. His FAR leg and far arm are in a noticeably darker shade. The two lifts must use DIFFERENT legs.
poses: NEAR FOOT LIFTED: the NEAR (lighter) foot lifted a few inches off the floor with the knee slightly bent; the FAR (darker) foot flat on the floor. Near arm bent and swinging forward, far arm bent and back.
PASSING: both feet close to the floor under the hips, standing nearly upright, near arm back and far arm forward, both arms bent.

FAR FOOT LIFTED: the FAR (darker) foot lifted a few inches off the floor with the knee slightly bent; the NEAR (lighter) foot planted flat. Far arm bent and forward, near arm bent and back. Clearly different from pose 1: the lifted foot is the darker one.
PASSING: both feet close to the floor, nearly upright, near arm forward and far arm back, both arms bent.
learned: First batch: the same (near) leg was lifted in both lift poses, so it read as hopping on one foot. Fix: name the near and far legs, shade the far one, and say 'the two lifts must use DIFFERENT legs'.
The model lifts the foot higher than the booklet's 4 inches. An edit pass ('lower the lifted foot to about 4 inches') brought it down; see edits.json.

attach: the previous sheet to fix: ex5-stationary-run.png
problems: The lifted foot rises far higher than the booklet's four inches and the stride is a jog. Make it a low march in place: the lifted shoe only about four inches off the floor (the sole of the lifted shoe just above the top of the planted shoe), the knee only slightly bent, the body upright, small steps, the arms bent about 90 degrees swinging gently.
Keep the rule that the two lifts use DIFFERENT legs: near (lighter) leg in pose 1, far (darker) leg in pose 3.
retake.keep: the boy's look, line weight and colors, four poses in the same order, the side-on body with the head and shoulders turned toward the camera, and the same angle in every pose.

scissor-jumps-c1.kept: take 1 of 4. Known weak spot: stance A and B look alike in profile; only shading differs
scissor-jumps-c1.layout: Same scale, wide empty gaps. The two standing poses rest on the same invisible floor line; the two jumping poses are drawn clearly higher, with both feet well above that line.
poses: STANCE A, on the floor: the leg NEAREST the viewer extended forward and the other leg extended backward in a wide scissor stance, both feet on the floor; the arm FARTHEST from the viewer extended forward and the near arm extended backward, both arms straight at SHOULDER HEIGHT.
JUMP, in the air: jumped straight up, both feet well off the floor, legs and arms passing each other mid-switch (legs close together under the hips, arms crossing near the body), knees slightly bent.

STANCE B, on the floor: the mirror of stance A. The leg FARTHEST from the viewer is now forward and the near leg is back; the NEAR arm extended forward and the far arm backward, arms straight at shoulder height, both feet on the floor.
JUMP, in the air: the same airborne switching pose as pose 2, both feet well above the floor line.
learned: Stance A and stance B look almost the same in profile; only the shading differs. A front view would fix it.
Stance B came out as a lunge with a bent back knee. An edit pass made it upright; see edits.json.
Batch C (2026-11-20): two camera rows came back almost identical and stance B was still indistinguishable from A. Remake in a single three-quarter front view with a stance diagram attached.

attach: the previous sheet to fix: ex5-scissor-jumps.png
problems: Stance A and stance B looked almost the same. They are mirror images: in stance A his RIGHT leg and LEFT arm are forward; in stance B his LEFT leg and RIGHT arm are forward. In a strict side view this is hard to see, so draw a three-quarter front view where the forward leg is clearly the one nearer the camera in A and the one farther from the camera in B.
One stance came out as a lunge. In both stances the front knee is only slightly bent, the back leg is STRAIGHT, the body upright, both arms straight at shoulder height (one forward, one back).
In the two jump poses both feet are clearly off the floor, the legs passing each other under the hips.
retake.keep: the boy's look, line weight and colors, four poses in the same order, the same scale, and the stances resting on one floor line with the jump poses clearly higher.
rows: three-quarter FRONT view, from the front and a little from the left, so that the forward and backward legs and arms can be told apart
SIDE view facing right with a clearly darker shade on the far arm and far leg
retake.why_rows: Scissor stances are hard to tell apart from the side, so this asks for two cameras; send me the whole image and I will pick the row that reads best.

check: Four poses: STANCE A, JUMP, STANCE B, JUMP
Stance A: right leg and left arm forward. Stance B: left leg and right arm forward. You can tell them apart without looking at shading
Back leg straight in both stances, no lunge
Both jump poses clearly higher than the stances, both feet off the floor

remake.schematic_note: a stick-figure diagram of the four poses seen from the side: which leg and which arm are forward in stance A and in stance B, and both feet off the floor in the jumps. Copy the positions only, never its style, colors or text.
remake.view: a THREE-QUARTER FRONT view: the body turned about 45 degrees toward the camera, facing right, so the viewer can see which leg and which arm are forward. The SAME angle in all four poses

toe-touch-c2.kept: Grok Imagine take, kept (5 figures: it added an extra bounce pose). Cycle start, touch, press, rebound, stretch back.
toe-touch-c2.layout: Same scale, feet on the same invisible floor line, with wide empty gaps so the figures never touch.
poses: START: standing tall, feet about shoulder-width apart, both arms straight up overhead, upper arms beside the ears.
TOUCH: deep forward bend, torso folded down toward the legs, knees only slightly bent (not forced straight, not deeply squatting), fingertips touching the floor beside the feet, head hanging relaxed.
PRESS: the same forward bend pressed one small bounce lower: fingertips pressing on the floor, torso and head a little lower than in the TOUCH pose, knees still only slightly bent.
STRETCH BACK: standing again with arms still stretched up and reaching backward, a gentle backward bend, hips pushed slightly forward, chest and face lifted toward the sky, knees straight.
check: Four poses, left to right
Knees only slightly bent in the two bends (not forced straight, not a squat)
Fingertips reach the floor in TOUCH and PRESS; PRESS is a little lower than TOUCH
In STRETCH BACK the arms are UP and back, not swept down behind him
draft: The booklet says 'touch floor and press (bounce) once'. Pose 3 (PRESS) is my reading of 'press once'. It differs only slightly from pose 2, so check it looks like a bounce, not a duplicate.
learned: Asked for 4 poses; Grok Imagine returned 5. Poses 2 and 3 are almost the same depth (3 px apart) and pose 4 is the real press (31 px lower), so the extra one works as the rebound after the press.
Pose 1 came back in a front-facing three-quarter view with the feet wide apart; the other four are side views. It matches 'feet astride' but is a camera change.
The author liked the slight turn toward the camera in the first figure (not a pure 90 degree side view). Later strips ask for it on purpose; see config/character.json 'view'.

sit-up-c2.kept: Grok Imagine, first take, kept as made (3 figures).
sit-up-c2.layout: In every pose he lies on his back with his HEAD ON THE LEFT and his FEET ON THE RIGHT, same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps so the figures never touch. Draw only the boy: no chair, no objects.
poses: START: lying flat on his back, legs straight on the floor with the feet about six inches apart, arms straight and resting at his sides.
RISING: halfway up, upper body lifted about 45 degrees off the floor, arms reaching forward, heels still on the floor, knees allowed to bend very slightly.

TOP: sitting up to a vertical position, back straight and upright, arms reaching forward toward the feet, FEET STAYING FLAT ON THE FLOOR, knees bent only slightly (hands NOT behind the head, heels NOT lifted).
check: Three poses, head on the left, feet on the right
Feet stay on the floor in every pose
TOP is a vertical, upright torso (this is a full sit-up, not the partial one in chart 1)
Knees at most slightly bent
Hands at the sides or reaching forward, not behind the head; no chair
draft: The booklet allows 'knees bend slightly' for this exercise. Chart 1's partial sit-up did not.
learned: Right on the first try: lying flat, rising to about 45 degrees, then a vertical torso with the arms reaching and the feet staying on the floor.
Anchored by the feet (span-right): the shorts wander 46 px across the poses. Anchoring by the hips would be steadier still.

back-extension-c2.kept: Grok Imagine, first take, kept as made (3 figures).
back-extension-c2.layout: In every pose he lies FACE DOWN, flat on his belly, with his HEAD ON THE RIGHT looking right and his FEET ON THE LEFT. Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps between figures.
back-extension-c2.rule: KEY BODY RULE FOR ALL THREE POSES: his arms are NOT pushing up and NOT planted in front of him. Both arms are STRAIGHT and stretched back along his sides, with the hands tucked flat, palms down, UNDER THE FRONT OF HIS THIGHS. Elbows straight.
poses: START: lying completely flat face down, legs straight and together, chin near the floor, arms straight back with palms under the thighs.
LIFTING: head, shoulders and both legs just beginning to lift off the floor together, legs straight, arms still straight back under the thighs.

TOP: head, shoulders AND BOTH LEGS raised off the floor at the same time, legs straight with the knees LOCKED, thighs clearly lifted off his hands, back gently arched, looking forward; only his belly stays on the floor.
check: Three poses, head on the right, feet on the left
Arms straight back, hands under the thighs (not planted in front like a push-up)
In TOP the head, shoulders and BOTH legs are up together
Legs straight, thighs clear of the hands
The hands are in the same place, under the front of the thighs, in all three poses
START, LIFTING and TOP are three clearly different heights
learned: Form is right: head, shoulders and both legs up, back gently arched, arms straight back, hands on the floor.
The leg raise is modest: the feet rise about 20 px more than at the start, so the thighs only just clear the hands. If a clearer raise is wanted, ask for 'legs raised high' or run an edit pass.
The START pose already has the feet a few pixels off the floor.

Both feet lift at the top, so a planted-foot anchor makes him slide 364 px. The new 'hips' anchor (the red shorts) holds him to 2 px. Use it for any exercise where he lies and the hips stay on the floor.
Batch C (2026-11-20): the lift improved but the hands moved forward to the hips, and START and LIFTING looked the same. Remake with the booklet drawing and a hands-and-thighs diagram attached.

attach: the previous sheet to fix: c2-ex3-back-extension.png
problems: The hands drifted forward to the hips and belly. Both hands stay flat on the floor UNDER THE FRONT OF THE THIGHS, just below the hips, fingers pointing toward the feet, arms straight back along the sides. They do not move between poses.
In TOP the thighs must lift clearly OFF the hands: a visible gap between the bottom of each thigh and the hand under it, the legs straight with the knees locked, the feet well above the floor.
START must lie completely flat (chest, thighs, shins and feet on the floor), and LIFTING must be clearly in between START and TOP. Earlier sheets drew START and LIFTING the same.
retake.keep: the boy's look, line weight and colors, three poses in the same order, head on the right and feet on the left, the same three-quarter view as the previous sheet.

remake.schematic_note: a stick-figure diagram of where the HANDS and THIGHS are in START and TOP, seen from the side. Copy the positions only, never its style, colors or text.

push-up-c2.exercise: a PUSH-UP (on the palms and toes, knees OFF the floor)
push-up-c2.kept: Grok Imagine, first take, kept as made (3 figures).
push-up-c2.layout: Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, with generous empty space between the figures so they do not touch or overlap.
poses: DOWN: face down with the chest touching the floor, palms flat on the floor directly under the shoulders, elbows bent and tucked close to the ribs, only the palms and the toes touching the floor, the body one straight line from head to heels.
MIDDLE: halfway up, elbows bent about 90 degrees, chest a hand-width above the floor, only the palms and toes touching the floor, body still one straight line, back straight.

UP: arms fully straightened, palms flat directly under the shoulders, only the palms and toes touching the floor, body one straight diagonal line from the heels to the head (hips NOT piked up, back NOT sagging, knees NOT on the floor).
check: Three poses, facing right
Only palms and toes touch the floor; knees are OFF the floor in every pose
Body a straight line, back straight (no sagging hips, no piked hips)
Chest touches the floor in DOWN; arms fully straight in UP
draft: This is a different exercise from chart 1's knee push-up. Grok's chart 1 push-up drew this form by mistake; here it is correct.
learned: Right on the first try, with the prompt unchanged: palms and toes only, knees off the floor, body one straight line, arms fully straight at the top.
The DOWN pose has the chest a hair above the floor rather than literally on it. At video size it reads as touching. The booklet says the chest must touch the floor, so look at this on a real screen.

astride-jumps-c2.kept: Grok Imagine, first take, kept as made (4 figures, front view).
astride-jumps-c2.view: strict FRONT view, the boy facing the camera (not a side view)
astride-jumps-c2.layout: Same scale, wide empty gaps so the figures never touch. The two standing poses rest on the same invisible floor line; the two jumping poses are drawn clearly higher, with both feet well above that line.
poses: START: standing with the FEET TOGETHER and the arms straight down at his sides.
JUMP OUT: in the air, both feet off the floor, legs spreading apart, arms swinging out sideways, arms straight.
LAND ASTRIDE: landed with the feet wide apart (astride), both feet flat on the floor, arms straight and raised sideways to slightly above shoulder height.
JUMP BACK: in the air, both feet off the floor, legs coming back together, arms coming down toward his sides, arms straight.
check: Four poses, strict front view, same boy
START has the feet together and the arms down
In LAND ASTRIDE the arms are straight and just above shoulder height, the feet wide apart
The two jump poses are clearly higher than the two standing poses
draft: Front view, because the legs and arms move sideways and a side view would hide it.
The booklet says 'return with a jump to the starting position for count of one', so one count is out AND back. I will decide how that maps to '10 astride jumps' when I wire it in.
learned: Right on the first try: feet together and arms down, jump out with the legs spread, land astride with the arms straight and above shoulder height, jump back.
The two jump poses sit about 89 px above the standing poses.

One count is taken to be a complete out-and-back (the booklet says 'return with a jump to the starting position for count of one'), so one cycle per count: jumps_per_cycle is 1 and a cycle takes 1.2 s. If the count should be each jump, set jumps_per_cycle to 2 in config/strips.json (2.4 s a cycle).

toe-touch-c3.exercise: TOE TOUCHES TO THE LEFT, CENTRE AND RIGHT
toe-touch-c3.view: strict FRONT view, the boy facing the camera (not a side view)
toe-touch-c3.layout: Same scale, feet on the same invisible floor line, with wide empty gaps so the figures never touch. The five figures are in the ORDER OF THE MOVEMENT, left to right across the picture, not in the order of where the hands land.
poses: START: standing tall facing the camera, feet wide apart (astride, a little wider than the shoulders), both arms straight up overhead, upper arms beside the ears.

TOUCH LEFT: bent forward at the waist, seen from the front, both hands reaching down together with the fingertips touching the floor about six inches OUTSIDE HIS LEFT FOOT (his left foot is on the RIGHT side of the picture), knees only slightly bent, head hanging down.
TOUCH BETWEEN: bent forward in the same way, fingertips of both hands touching the floor BETWEEN HIS FEET, pressing down a little, knees only slightly bent, head hanging down.

TOUCH RIGHT: bent forward in the same way, fingertips of both hands touching the floor about six inches OUTSIDE HIS RIGHT FOOT (his right foot is on the LEFT side of the picture), knees only slightly bent, head hanging down.
BEND BACK: standing again, feet still wide apart, both arms stretched up and back, bending backward as far as he can, hips pushed forward, chest and face lifted toward the sky, knees straight.
check: Five poses in movement order
Front view in every pose, feet wide apart throughout
TOUCH LEFT: fingertips on the floor outside his left foot (the picture-right foot); TOUCH RIGHT: outside his right foot (the picture-left foot); TOUCH BETWEEN: between the feet
Knees only slightly bent in the three bends
BEND BACK: arms up and back, leaning backward as far as he can
draft: Front view, because the three touches land at different places across the floor and a side view would hide that.
Left and right are the boy's own: his left foot is on the right side of the picture when he faces us.

The booklet says to reverse the direction after half the number of counts (right, between, left in the second half). That needs no extra picture: I will run the same poses in reverse order in the build.
If the generator struggles with a bend seen from the front, try 'three-quarter front view' instead, and tell me.

sit-up-hands-behind-head-c3.exercise: a SIT-UP WITH THE HANDS CLASPED BEHIND THE HEAD
sit-up-hands-behind-head-c3.layout: In every pose he lies on his back with his HEAD ON THE LEFT and his FEET ON THE RIGHT, same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps so the figures never touch. Draw only the boy: no chair, no objects.
poses: START: lying flat on his back, legs straight on the floor with the feet about six inches apart, fingers clasped behind his head with the elbows out to the sides.
RISING: halfway up, upper body lifted about 45 degrees off the floor, hands still clasped behind his head with the elbows wide, heels still on the floor, knees allowed to bend very slightly.

TOP: sitting up to a vertical position, back straight and upright, hands still clasped behind his head with the elbows wide, FEET STAYING FLAT ON THE FLOOR, knees bent only slightly (hands NOT reaching forward, heels NOT lifted).
check: Three poses, head on the left, feet on the right
Fingers clasped behind the head in ALL three poses (the arms do not reach forward)
Feet stay on the floor; TOP is a vertical, upright torso
Knees at most slightly bent; no chair
draft: The same exercise as chart 2's sit-up, with the hands clasped behind the head.

back-extension-hands-behind-back-c3.exercise: a BACK EXTENSION WITH THE HANDS INTERLOCKED BEHIND THE BACK
back-extension-hands-behind-back-c3.layout: In every pose he lies FACE DOWN, flat on his belly, with his HEAD ON THE RIGHT looking right and his FEET ON THE LEFT. Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps between figures.
back-extension-hands-behind-back-c3.rule: KEY BODY RULE FOR ALL THREE POSES: his hands are INTERLOCKED BEHIND HIS BACK, fingers clasped over the lower back, arms straight. His hands are NOT under his thighs, NOT in front of him and NOT on the floor.
poses: START: lying completely flat face down, legs straight and together, chin near the floor, hands interlocked behind the back.
LIFTING: head, shoulders, chest and both legs just beginning to lift off the floor together, legs straight, hands still interlocked behind the back.

TOP: head, shoulders, chest AND BOTH THIGHS lifted completely off the floor, as high as he can, legs straight with the knees LOCKED, back strongly arched, looking forward, hands still interlocked behind the back; only his lower belly and hips stay on the floor.
check: Three poses, head on the right, feet on the left
Hands interlocked behind the back in ALL three poses (not under the thighs, not on the floor)
TOP: chest AND both thighs clear of the floor, higher than chart 2's back extension
Legs straight
draft: Chart 2's back extension kept the hands on the floor under the thighs. Here the hands are clasped behind the back, so the lift can go higher.

chin-forehead-push-up-c3.exercise: a CHIN-FOREHEAD PUSH-UP (on the palms and toes, knees OFF the floor)
chin-forehead-push-up-c3.layout: Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, with generous empty space between the figures so they do not touch or overlap.
poses: UP: arms fully straightened, palms flat directly under the shoulders, only the palms and toes touching the floor, the body one straight line from the heels to the head (hips NOT piked up, back NOT sagging, knees NOT on the floor).

CHIN: lowered until the CHIN touches the floor in front of the hands (the head pushed forward past the hands), elbows bent, palms still flat on the floor under the shoulders, only the palms, toes and chin touching the floor, the body one straight line.

FOREHEAD (a PIKE, as in the booklet's drawing): the hips pushed UP HIGH so the body makes an upside-down V, the palms still flat on the floor where they were, the elbows bent, the head tucked down and back between the arms so the FOREHEAD touches the floor just BEHIND the hands (on the feet side of the hands), the toes on the floor. Only the palms, the toes and the forehead touch the floor. This pose is NOT a straight body: the hips are the highest point.
check: Three poses, facing right: UP, CHIN, FOREHEAD
UP: arms straight, body one straight line, knees off the floor
CHIN: body low and straight, the chin on the floor IN FRONT of the hands, the head ahead of the hands
FOREHEAD: hips high in an upside-down V (a pike), the forehead on the floor BEHIND the hands, hands ahead of the forehead
The three poses are clearly different at a glance
draft: The booklet does not say whether this push-up is on the toes or the knees. I assumed palms and toes, continuing chart 2. If it should be the knees, tell me and I will change one phrase.
'Forehead on the floor behind the hands' is physically awkward. If Grok's FOREHEAD pose is not clearly different from CHIN, send me what it gives and I will check it against the booklet.
The booklet stresses three separate movements (chin, forehead, arms straightened), not one continuous one. The build will hold each pose.

attach: the previous sheet to fix: c3-ex234-sit-back-push.png (use only its bottom row, the push-up)
problems: In the FOREHEAD pose the forehead landed IN FRONT of the hands. The forehead touches the floor BEHIND the hands. The way to get it there is a PIKE, as in the booklet drawing: hips up high, head tucked down between the arms.
The CHIN pose must be clearly lower than UP: the chin touching the floor in front of the hands, the head pushed forward past the hands, the elbows bent, the body low and straight.
retake.keep: the boy's look, line weight and colors, three poses in the same order, palms and toes only (knees off the floor), the body one straight line, and the feet on one floor line.
rows: plain SIDE view facing right, with both hands visible at the ends of the arms
three-quarter FRONT view, from the front and a little from one side, so that the head and the hands can be seen clearly
retake.why_rows: The forehead-behind-the-hands pose is hard to draw, so this asks for two cameras; send me the whole image and I will pick the row that shows it.
poses: UP: arms fully straightened, palms flat directly under the shoulders, only the palms and toes touching the floor, the body one straight line from the heels to the head (hips NOT piked up, back NOT sagging, knees NOT on the floor).

CHIN: lowered until the CHIN touches the floor in front of the hands (the head pushed forward past the hands), elbows bent, palms still flat on the floor under the shoulders, only the palms, toes and chin touching the floor, the body one straight line.

FOREHEAD: lowered until the chest is almost on the floor, the head tucked down and back so that the FOREHEAD touches the floor between the hands, level with the line of the hands or slightly behind it (the hands are visibly AHEAD of the forehead, in the direction he is facing), the elbows bent and flared out, the palms flat, only the palms, toes and forehead touching the floor, the body one straight line.

learned: Batch C (2026-11-20): our FOREHEAD wording (body straight, chest almost on the floor) contradicted the booklet. The booklet drawing (5BX figures/c3e4.png) shows the forehead pose as a pike: hips high, head tucked between the arms, which is how the forehead gets behind the hands. Rewritten to match; attach the booklet drawing.

half-knee-bends-c3.layout: Same scale, all three figures standing on the same invisible floor line (the toes of the third figure stay on that line while the heels lift), with wide empty gaps so the figures never touch.
poses: START: standing upright, feet together, hands on the hips, back straight.

HALF BEND: knees bent to an angle of about 110 degrees (a HALF bend, NOT a deep squat, knees NOT bent past a right angle), back upright and straight, hands on the hips, both feet flat on the floor, feet together.

RISE: straightened to a fully upright position and raised UP ON THE TOES, the heels lifted off the floor and the toes still touching the floor, legs straight, back upright and straight, hands on the hips.

pike-sit-up-c6.exercise: a PIKE SIT-UP: sitting up and lifting both legs at the same time to touch the toes in a V
pike-sit-up-c6.view: strict SIDE view, the boy facing right, with the SAME camera angle in every pose
pike-sit-up-c6.layout: In every pose he lies on his back (or sits) with his HEAD ON THE LEFT and his FEET ON THE RIGHT, same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps so the figures never touch. Draw only the boy: no chair, no objects.
poses: START: lying flat on his back, legs straight and the feet together, both arms stretched straight over the head along the floor.
RISING: the upper body and BOTH straight legs lifting off the floor together about halfway, arms reaching forward toward the toes, feet together.

PIKE: balanced on his seat in a V shape, the upper body AND both straight legs lifted clear of the floor, the arms straight and the fingertips touching the toes, feet together, legs and arms straight.

back-extension-press-c6.exercise: a BACK EXTENSION WITH A PRESS BACK

back-extension-press-c6.layout: In every pose he lies FACE DOWN, flat on his belly, with his HEAD ON THE LEFT and his FEET ON THE RIGHT. Same scale, all on the same invisible floor line, wide empty gaps between figures.

PRESS: from the top, one extra small push BACK and UP: the arms, chest and legs a little higher still, the back arched a little further, still with the arms and legs straight.

semi-spread-eagle-jumps-c5.view: strict FRONT view, the boy facing the camera (not a side view)
